title: Interpreting the Effects of DNA Polymerase Variants at the Structural Level Using MAVISp and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
authors: Arnaudi M; Krzesińska K; Beltrame L; Besora PS; Tiberti M; Nilbert M; Rohlin A; Papaleo E
one_liner_zh: 该文用MAVISp框架和分子动力学模拟分析DNA聚合酶POLE/POLD1的错义变异对折叠、稳定性和DNA结合的影响，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作和MD方法，但对象为聚合酶而非转录因子，且侧重变异解读而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，故为中档匹配。
abstract: Genetic variants in the DNA polymerase enzymes POLE and POLD1 can affect protein function by altering stability, catalysis, DNA binding, and interactions with other biomolecules. Understanding the structural basis of these variants is important for a comprehensive interpretation of variant impact. In this study, we used MAVISp, a modular structure-based framework, and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze over 60,000 missense variants of POLE and POLD1. By integrating results from changes in folding and binding free energies, local alterations in the proximity of the active or phosphorylation sites, we provided a detailed structural interpretation of variants reported across various databases, including ClinVar, COSMIC, and cBioPortal. Moreover, we predicted the functional consequences of variants not found yet in disease-related databases, thereby creating a comprehensive catalogue for future studies. Of note, our approach enabled us to classify 364 Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS) as PP3 evidence and 323 as BP4 evidence, in accordance with the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines. Additionally, we identified a group of variants that could alter the native orientation of the residues within the catalytic site of the exonuclease domain, such as POLE variants P297S and P436R. Finally, we identified a group of variants predicted to affect DNA-binding affinity and rationalized their effects in terms of different energetic contributions and structural features. Collectively, our results not only advance our understanding of protein variant effects in POLE and POLD1 at the structural level but also support future studies aimed at variant classification, variant prioritization for experimental studies, and functional interpretation across diverse biological contexts.
abstract_zh: DNA聚合酶POLE和POLD1中的遗传变异可通过改变蛋白质稳定性、催化活性、DNA结合能力及与其他生物分子的相互作用来影响蛋白质功能。理解这些变异的结构基础对于全面解读变异影响至关重要。在本研究中，我们利用MAVISp（一种基于模块的结构框架）和分子动力学模拟，分析了POLE和POLD1中超过60,000个错义变异。通过整合折叠自由能和结合自由能变化的结果，以及活性位点或磷酸化位点附近的局部改变，我们对来自ClinVar、COSMIC和cBioPortal等多个数据库报告的变异提供了详细的结构解读。此外，我们预测了尚未在疾病相关数据库中发现的变异的功能后果，从而为未来研究创建了一个全面目录。值得注意的是，我们的方法使我们能够根据美国医学遗传学与基因组学学会（ACMG）指南，将364个意义不明确的变异（VUS）分类为PP3证据，323个分类为BP4证据。另外，我们识别出一组可能改变外切酶结构域催化位点内残基天然取向的变异，例如POLE变异P297S和P436R。最后，我们识别出一组预测影响DNA结合亲和力的变异，并从不同能量贡献和结构特征的角度合理化了它们的影响。总体而言，我们的结果不仅增进了我们在结构水平上对POLE和POLD1蛋白质变异效应的理解，还为未来旨在变异分类、实验研究变异优先级排序以及跨多种生物学背景的功能解读的研究提供了支持。
